Article Title: 'Now that Nitish is no longer there': Expelled Anant Singh says has no regrets, to float own party
Article Text:
‘No distance between me and Nitish’: Anant Singh after JD(U) expels him, wife

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Expelled Janata Dal (United) strongman Anant Singh on Sunday claimed the Nitish Kumar 's party is “finished” after his expulsion, predicting that it would fail to win even 10 seats in the next election.The Mokama MLA and Nitish Kumar loyalist also said he had “no regrets” over the action and maintained that he shared a cordial relationship with Nitish Kumar.Anant Singh's remarks came a day after the JD(U), which has been in power in Bihar for nearly two decades under Nitish Kumar’s leadership, expelled him and his wife, Neelam Devi , for six years over alleged “anti-party” activities.Speaking to reporters, Singh said he would form his own political party and questioned the future of the JD(U) after Nitish Kumar’s exit from Bihar throne and move away from an active role in state politics.“The party belonged to Nitish Kumar. Now that Nitish Kumar is no longer there (in the active role), what is left of the party? Who among those in the leadership-- the ones who expelled me—has actually contributed anything?... Now, they will not even get 10 seats... Why will I go anywhere? I will simply build my own party,” he said.“The JD(U) is finished. Once they hold elections, everything will become clear,” Mokama MLA added.Despite his criticism of the party, Singh denied any rift with Nitish Kumar, saying, “There is no distance between me and Nitish-ji; we maintain a cordial relationship. I will go and visit him sometime -- there’s no issue. Let them keep their party; it serves no real purpose anyway.”“I will simply build my own party... I have no regrets. Whatever action has been taken, it’s fine; I have no issues with it,” he said.The JD(U) had accused Anant Singh of repeatedly disobeying the party leadership and using inappropriate and insulting language against its senior leaders.In a further move, the party has approached Bihar Legislative Assembly Speaker Prem Kumar seeking Singh’s disqualification as an MLA under the Tenth Schedule of the Constitution, commonly known as the anti-defection law.
Article Summary: Mokama MLA and Nitish Kumar loyalist Anant Singh said he would form his own political party. Singh's remarks came a day after the JD(U) expelled him and his wife, Neelam Devi, for six years over alleged “anti-party” activities.

Article Title: Patrick Mahomes and Brittany Mahomes’ $325 million KC Current extend historic unbeaten home run to 31 matches
Article Text:
Patrick Mahomes and Brittany Mahomes (Getty Images)

Patrick Mahomes and Brittany Mahomes’ KC Current eye home playoff advantage

KC Current rely on Temwa Chawinga and Croix Bethune before Decision Day

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

The Kansas City Current have another postseason to prepare for, giving owners Patrick Mahomes and Brittany Mahomes another reason to celebrate their investment in women’s soccer. The club has secured its third consecutive National Women’s Soccer League playoff berth, overcoming a season of major changes to remain among the league’s contenders. However, qualification is only the first step. With home-field advantage still up for grabs, Kansas City faces an important final stretch that could shape its chances of making a deep postseason run.The Current officially secured their playoff place after the Portland Thorns defeated the North Carolina Courage 1-0 on Friday night, October 23. Kansas City, Utah Royals and Portland Thorns each have 47 points, placing the three clubs in the playoff picture.For Patrick Mahomes and Brittany Mahomes, who are part of the Current’s ownership group, the achievement reflects the club’s continued competitiveness despite a challenging campaign.Kansas City will host the Washington Spirit on Sunday, October 25, in its final home match of the regular season. The match carries extra importance because a victory could strengthen the Current’s chances of earning a top-four seed and hosting a playoff game.The club also hopes to welcome 18,000 supporters for its annual fan appreciation match, potentially setting another attendance record. Strong home support has been a defining feature of Kansas City’s season, with the team remaining unbeaten across 31 consecutive home matches, an NWSL record.Head coach Chris Armas has faced a demanding first season in charge of a women’s team. Roster changes and shifting availability have tested the squad, but the Current have continued to collect important results.Kansas City’s home form has helped offset its inconsistent results away from home. The team has recorded a 10-0-4 home record, compared with a 4-1-9 mark on the road.The Current have scored 50 goals this season, including 37 at home. Temwa Chawinga remains a major attacking threat, leading the team with 12 goals despite missing matches through injury and international duty.Croix Bethune has also made a significant impact. Her 10 assists have matched the NWSL single-season record, which she shares with Utah’s Cloé Lacasse.The next challenge will be maintaining that momentum when the regular season concludes. On Decision Day, November 1, Kansas City will face Racing Louisville, currently 15th in the standings. All 16 teams are scheduled to play at 4 p.m. Central Time.The NWSL playoffs begin with the quarterfinals from November 6 to 8. For the Mahomes-owned club, securing a favourable seed could provide a valuable advantage as it pursues another postseason run.
Article Summary: KC Current have secured their third consecutive National Women’s Soccer League playoff berth. Kansas City will host the Washington Spirit on Sunday, October 25, in its final home match of the regular season. The club has recorded a 10-0-4 home record, compared with a 4-1-9 mark on the road.

Article Title: Travis Kelce’s $5.35 million estate faces another setback as neighbors challenge his landscaping plans
Article Text:
Travis Kelce mansion (Getty Images)

Travis Kelce’s $5.35 million mansion faces another planning hurdle

Travis Kelce’s landscaping plans spark wider neighborhood concerns

Travis Kelce’s $5.35 million Ohio mansion has become the centre of a growing neighborhood dispute, with concerns about privacy, property boundaries and the look of the lakefront estate complicating his plans. The Kansas City Chiefs star has faced fresh resistance from residents in Bratenahl, where local officials have approved parts of the proposed landscaping but rejected other elements. Despite efforts to address objections, the project remains unfinished, forcing Kelce’s team to revisit its plans as tensions with longtime neighbors continue to simmer.The dispute surrounding Kelce’s luxury property has taken another turn after a village review board declined to approve trees proposed along the shoreline. Officials also placed conditions on parts of the front landscaping, leaving the project with more work to complete before the estate’s outdoor plans can move forward.Kelce’s property in Bratenahl, near Cleveland, spans approximately 21,000 square feet and includes eight bedrooms, 11 bathrooms, a guest cottage, a swimming pool and a converted ballroom and game room. The scale of the estate has brought added attention to plans for privacy and landscaping in the established lakeside community.The proposed six-foot aluminum fence has also drawn objections. Residents raised concerns about its appearance, its potential effect on wildlife and whether it would provide meaningful protection from unwanted attention. One neighbor warned that deer could become trapped on the fence’s pointed tops.The review process has highlighted the challenge of balancing a high-profile homeowner’s security needs with local rules designed to protect lake views, neighborhood character and property values.Sewer infrastructure remains one of the concerns raised by neighboring residents, but it is not the only issue holding up the project.Katherine Bolton, who has lived next door for 35 years, questioned plans to plant around 50 evergreen trees near an old clay sewer line. She said the roots could cause serious damage and cited a potential $75,000 repair bill for lining the pipe.“Planting 50 evergreen trees just ten feet from a 100-year-old clay sewer line is virtually guaranteed to cause severe root intrusion, pipe structural failure, and catastrophic sewage backups,” she said, citing AI-based research.Kelce’s construction team has pushed back by pointing to changes made in response to residents’ complaints. Project representative Jacob Kutz said the owners had already paid $7,500 to repair a damaged section of the sewer line without seeking contributions from the neighbors.The team also moved the fence two feet inside the property boundary, added access gates and paid to trim trees on neighboring land.Those adjustments have not resolved every disagreement. The board has allowed some landscaping work but wants a revised proposal for the shoreline trees.For Kelce, the next step is to return with a plan that addresses the remaining objections while meeting the village’s requirements. Until then, the mansion’s landscaping project remains caught between private property plans and the expectations of the surrounding community.
Article Summary: Travis Kelce’s $5.35 million Ohio mansion has become the centre of a growing neighborhood dispute. Concerns about privacy, property boundaries and the look of the lakefront estate complicating his plans. The Kansas City Chiefs star has faced fresh resistance from residents in Bratenahl.

Article Title: Interview | ‘AAP had 4.5 years to end drug menace, gangsterism in Punjab’: Sachin Pilot
Article Text:
"Drug menace and underworld-crime are top issues in the upcoming elections," Sachin Pilot said.

Drug menace and underworld-crime are top issues in the upcoming elections in

Punjab

. AAP has shown no will to root them out, says Congress, but if voted to office, it will finish these off, AICC state in-charge

Sachin Pilot

Where does Congress think the AAP govt has failed in Punjab?

Congress made you in-charge of Punjab in the context of infighting in the state unit with elections just five months away. And then it also changed its state chief Amrinder Singh Raja Warring.

"In Punjab, there are record Dalit atrocities, unemployment and persistent agrarian crisis," Pilot said.

BJP is also slamming the AAP govt over drug menace.

It will be a four-cornered contest between AAP, Congress, BJP and SAD.

Will Congress project a CM face in Punjab?

■ The top issue is the menace of drugs. The mafia and bureaucratic nexus is so overwhelming that home delivery of drugs is much quicker than home delivery of food. It’s ‘chitta’. As per NCRB 2024, Punjab had the second highest NDPS Act crime rate at 29 cases per lakh. If AAP govt had the will to finish off the drug menace, it would have done so in 4.5 years. Look at gangsterism, the nexus between people in jail and those operating outside carrying out shootouts, robberies. This had never been the culture of Punjab, even in its darkest hour. You never had homegrown gangs operating in public. Narco money feeds gang operations. Police/intelligence do not have the integrity and the political direction to curb this menace. These twin evils lead to unemployment. In Punjab, there are record Dalit atrocities, unemployment and persistent agrarian crisis. The AAP failure is taking the state downhill.■Punjab is an important state not just for Congress, but also for the country. Its contribution — historical, political, social — is there for all to see. We are confident that the people of Punjab are looking for a change and Congress will provide that change.There may be different viewpoints, but there are no factions in the Punjab Congress. We are fighting unitedly to oust the AAP govt. Changes in the organisation are routine exercises.■Punjab is a border state and all the drugs are coming from across the border which is the responsibility of the Union ministry of home affairs and the defence ministry. So, it is wholly farcical when BJP launches an anti-drug drive in Punjab. What have they done to curb the menace on the borders of Rajasthan, Punjab and Gujarat. Mundra Port recorded the highest seizure of cocaine in history — Rs 21,000 crore in one consignment in 2021. Imagine how much cocaine would have slipped through unnoticed. BJP has to answer these questions.■The main contest is between AAP and Congress. Of the 13 Lok Sabha seats in 2024 polls, Congress won seven. BJP has no strong footing in Punjab and has survived on the back of SAD support. But SAD has also split and is facing internal issues. It is not the force like they were under Badal Senior. It will be a bipolar contest over who can lead Punjab better. There will be other players like Amritpal Singh’s party, but people of Punjab don’t give a fractured mandate. Congress played the role of a strong opposition for 4.5 years while others were missing. When in office, Congress has delivered in the past.■ Congress has never given the CM faces. There is a state president, campaign committee chairman, a legislature party leader — a whole lot of people who fight as a team.
Article Summary: "Drug menace and underworld-crime are top issues in the upcoming elections," Sachin Pilot said. Punjab will be a four-cornered contest between AAP, Congress, BJP and SAD, he said. Article Title: Suspicious pigeon with coded ring, Pak currency causes a flutter in Jammu
Article Text:
A police team arrived soon and seized the pigeon with the items. (File photo)

JAMMU: A suspicious pigeon carrying a coded ring, a chit written in Urdu and Pakistani currency was caught by locals along the border in Jammu’s Samba district on Saturday, officials said.An official pointed out that such episodes are not uncommon in border areas of J&K and Punjab, where pigeons have been used for smuggling or for sending messages across the frontier.On Saturday, the pigeon was found near a temple in Samba’s border area of Mawa around 6.40am and was immediately captured by locals after they spotted a ring tied to its leg. “A ring bearing Code No 03341214150 was found attached to its leg, besides the note and currency,” the official said.A police team arrived soon and seized the pigeon with the items. “The pigeon has been taken for examination. Security agencies are verifying the contents of the note and the origin of the bird,” the official said.Suspicious creatures and items flying in are not a rarity in Jammu’s border zones. On Friday, a balloon bearing the marking of Pakistan International Airlines (PIA) was found near a border post in Ghou Manhasan. This sparked a search of the area as a precautionary measure. On Oct 17, a suspicious aircraft-shaped balloon bearing the PIA symbol was seized from Jammu’s Khaur area.
Article Summary: A suspicious pigeon carrying a coded ring, a chit written in Urdu and Pakistani currency was caught by locals along the border in Jammu’s Samba district on Saturday. Such episodes are not uncommon in border areas of J&K and Punjab, where pigeons have been used for smuggling.

Article Title: Why do some women become the strongest defenders of patriarchy
Article Text:
Delhi University women took to streets demanding safety after news report of a gangrape near a girls college.

“Sir, let me say that I am not a feminist. I consider myself as a human being. As a human being we feel that it is our duty to help women, minorities, Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes, OBCs, and also the neglected class.” Mamata Banerjee in Lok Sabha on Women’s Day, 2008.

Oxford dictionary defines

feminism

as 'the belief and aim that women should have the same rights and opportunities as men or the struggle to achieve this aim.'

Why do some women keep patriarchy alive

Azaadi

Oxford dictionary defines patriarchy as '​a society, system or country that is ruled or controlled by men.'

Is the 'aurat hi aurat ki dushman' concept real?

From 'mere sar mei dard hai, iska karan marrd hai' to 'ek sutta, 2 chai, marrd jaat haye haye', the protest saw viral slogans. (PTI image)

Can patriarchy give women a sense of power?

When tradition becomes a question of freedom

When women challenge the rules they grew up with

kutta nahi sher bano

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Patriarchy gives some women a sense of belonging

Then why is it that some of us distance ourselves from this term? And why is it that some women uphold the very patriarchy that restricts them?A group called the NCMIndia Council for Men Affairs recently took out a 'Long Live Patriarchy' march that went viral on social media. The group also had women holding the banner. "In the name of equality, these girls don't want to do jhaadu-pocha, clean utensils or raise kids. They just want freedom, money and debauchery," one of the women at the march said. "Equality does not mean freedom to drink, smoke, roam around at night. Women are misusing their independence.does not mean shaming men."TOI spoke to Dolly Kumari, who is also a member of the group that actively raises men's issues, and asked her what patriarchy meant to her."Patriarchy cannot be understood simply as a system created by men to oppress women. When a woman speaks about men's issues, some people may find it surprising because they expect her to speak only from a particular gender-based perspective. But I do not believe empathy should have a gender. Supporting men who experience injustice does not mean denying the difficulties women face," she said."My objection is to the idea that everything traditional must be condemned as patriarchal and, therefore, bad. If a man wants to protect and provide for his family, and a woman willingly chooses to trust him in that role, why should society automatically call that oppression or brainwashed women?"It would appear, then, that women supporting patriarchy would be an anomaly. However, Dolly said that the purpose of their 'Long Live Patriarchy' initiative was to raise awareness of men's rights, which "we have been organising on Gandhi Jayanti for nearly a decade.""Equality should not become a competition between men and women. Women deserve justice, and so do men. We need a society where both can express their pain, seek support, and live with dignity without being judged by gender stereotypes," said Dolly."In the traditional Indian family, men were often expected to provide, protect and take responsibility for their families while women traditionally took on many responsibilities related to the home and children. These roles evolved within the social and economic realities of their time although it resulted in unequal rights and restrictions. Our history is not simply a story of oppression and therefore patriarchy should prevail. "Does different treatment of a son from daughter and parenting play a role in keeping misogyny alive? Or is this 'aurat hi aurat ki dushman hoti hai' syndrome.Devika Anand, a psychologist at Rise and Mind, believes that the answer lies partly in the way gender roles are normalised within families and communities."I think one way to understand this is that we don't always question the systems we grow up in, particularly when those systems are presented to us as normal, moral, or necessary. When a woman grows up learning that a good woman is one who sacrifices, adjusts, tolerates, or puts others before herself, these expectations can become deeply embedded in her understanding of what it means to be a woman," she said.Over time, these expectations may stop feeling like restrictions and start being seen as values. A woman may even derive a sense of identity or self-worth from having lived up to them, sometimes at considerable personal cost."When younger women choose differently, it can challenge not just her beliefs but also the meaning she has attached to her own sacrifices," Devika explained.This explains why some women who have experienced restrictions themselves may go on to impose similar expectations on younger women. Having spent years adjusting to restrictive norms, they may come to regard them as an inevitable part of life rather than something that can be challenged."There can also be a need to make sense of one's own experiences. If someone has made significant sacrifices because she believed there was no alternative, acknowledging that those sacrifices were unnecessary or unfair can be painful. It may bring up feelings of anger, grief, or regret. Believing that younger women must make similar sacrifices can sometimes help preserve the sense that those sacrifices had a purpose," Devika said.When certain expectations are repeatedly reinforced within families and communities, they can become the default way of relating to others. A woman may reproduce the same expectations she experienced, not necessarily because she wants younger women to suffer, but because she has learned to see those expectations as responsible or appropriate behaviour."Power doesn't always mean having equal power within a system. Sometimes, it means having more power than someone else within that system," Devika said.In a patriarchal family, a woman may have limited autonomy in relation to men but still hold considerable authority over younger women, daughters-in-law or other women in the household. She may have little influence over the rules themselves but gain status by enforcing them."This can give her a sense of belonging, security, or control in an environment where her own power is otherwise limited," Devika explained.There can also be a psychological incentive to conform. If a woman receives approval, respect or recognition for upholding family traditions, questioning those traditions may threaten not only her beliefs but also her position within the family or community.Calling kindness, compassion, empathy and nurture 'qualities' that women should have, Dolly said, "I feel that relationships are increasingly being discussed in terms of personal freedom, sometimes without equal emphasis on duties, compromise, commitment, and mutual accountability."Dolly believes that a woman does not have to reject tradition to prove that she is empowered. "I come from a traditional, patriarchal family, yet my father always encouraged me to participate in activities that people might traditionally associate with boys. I played sports, learned to ride a bike, built a career in technology, and today have a beautiful family of my own. Growing up with two brothers also gave me a personal experience of sharing opportunities and responsibilities across gender lines. That experience is one of the reasons I believe that having a traditional father or growing up in a strict household does not automatically mean being oppressed. Tradition and discipline are not inherently oppressive," she said.Devika, too, cautions against labelling every woman who holds a traditional belief as a victim of internalised misogyny, which may include judging women more harshly than men, policing other women's behaviour, or believing that women are inherently less capable or less deserving of autonomy.A 65-year old influencer from Haryana called Tai Savitri, who recently went viral over her commentary on society and patriarchy, told TOI that even though her experiences have been bitter, it was her educated children that taught her to become a feminist. "I was less educated. My kids got good education so I learnt a few things from them. It was also a feeling that I should do something for the women," she told TOI.She recalled facing criticism in her village, even though her family did not offer much resistance to her views."Yes, I have also heard that aurat hi aurat ki dushman hoti hai but I think it is more because of lack of education that pitied one woman against the other, a system wherein one woman was the slave of another. This created a scenario where women did not want other women to succeed in life," she said.In one of her viral videos, Savitri compared women who restrict other women to dogs that have become accustomed to living on a leash. "You must have seen dog owners taking their pets out. Even if they let go of this leash, by mistake or deliberately, you will notice that the dog itself will hold the leash in his mouth and give it back to his owner. Because the dog has now developed a habit of living like a slave and it has accepted its fate. It is the same with women who try to show other women in poor light. It is the same slave mentality. My only message to women is(don't be a dog, be a tiger). Whoever tries to put a leash on you or make you a slave, rip them to shreds," she said.There is a distinction between having a choice and the freedom to make that choice. Holding a traditional belief is not the same as denying another woman the right to choose differently. The consequences of that belief, and the degree to which it is imposed on others, matter.Women who defend patriarchal expectations are not necessarily motivated by a single cause. Their views may be shaped by the values they grew up with, the sacrifices they have made, the security they derive from their place within a family or community, or a genuine belief that traditional arrangements offer stability.The question, then, is not simply why some women become flagbearers of patriarchy. It is also why a system that can restrict women's choices sometimes offers them identity, belonging or authority in return—and what it would take for women to feel secure enough to question it.Perhaps the more useful question is not whether women are their own enemies, but whether a society that teaches women to measure their worth through sacrifice, obedience and conformity gives them enough room to imagine a different way of living.
Article Summary: A group called the NCMIndia Council for Men Affairs recently took out a 'Long Live Patriarchy' march that went viral on social media. The group also had women holding the banner. ToI spoke to Dolly Kumari, who is also a member of the group that actively raises men's issues, and asked what patriarchy meant to her.

Article Title: ‘Sri Lanka, Bangladesh happen when protests are not allowed’: Sonam Wangchuk on anti-SIR stir crackdown
Article Text:

(With PTI inputs)

NEW DELHI: Activist Sonam Wangchuk on Saturday described protests as a “great mechanism” for governments to improve their performance, citing the unrest in Sri Lanka and Bangladesh as examples of what could happen when demonstrations are not allowed.“Nations all around the world happily permit protests, and that too right in front of Parliament. In countries like the UK, Norway and Sweden, protests are allowed right in front of Parliament,” the educationist said at an event in Mumbai.“In India, it was far from Parliament. Even when it was just Jantar Mantar, it was too far,” he added.Wangchuk was referring to demonstrations held at Delhi’s Jantar Mantar, the capital’s now-denotified designated protest site, in June and July following the NEET-UG paper leak in May.The protests, in which Wangchuk played a key role by undertaking an indefinite fast for over 20 days before being removed and taken to a hospital, ended with the resignation of then-Union education minister Dharmendra Pradhan on July 25.His remarks came amid ongoing protests in Delhi demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar over alleged irregularities in the Special Intensive Revision of electoral rolls.The Centre deployed extensive security measures, drawing criticism from opposition parties.“Look what happens when protests are not allowed. That is the example of Sri Lanka, Bangladesh,” Wangchuk remarked, referring to the youth- and student-led demonstrations in Sri Lanka and Bangladesh that culminated in the ouster of the incumbent governments.“If you (the Centre) do things that need not be done, people will turn against you. This will only hurt the government. Do what is right,” he stated.The movements in Sri Lanka and Bangladesh were also cited by several opposition leaders, civil society members and student leaders, some of whom called for “regime change” in India along the lines of the two neighbouring countries. After the ruling BJP seized on these remarks, alleging that the anti-CEC protesters’ real intention was to topple the democratically-elected Modi government, the leaders clarified that they were advocating "regime change through elections. "Delhi Police has also made several protesters sign peace bonds, undertaking to maintain "peace and good behaviour."
Article Summary: Wangchuk was referring to demonstrations held at Delhi’s Jantar Mantar in June and July following the NEET-UG paper leak in May. His remarks came amid ongoing protests in Delhi demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over alleged irregularities.

Article Title: Daughter’s inheritance rights can’t be defeated by limitation: J&K and Ladakh high court
Article Text:
The dispute dates back to Sept 14, 1982

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

JAMMU: The high court of Jammu & Kashmir and Ladakh has restored a woman’s right to inherit her father’s property after a 44-year-long legal battle, holding that an adverse revenue entry recorded during when she was a minor cannot automatically defeat a legitimate inheritance claim on limitation grounds.The dispute dates back to Sept 14, 1982, when Themu, daughter of late Sonu, filed a civil suit claiming half share in land measuring 58 kanals and 11 marlas left behind by her father.She challenged mutation no. 43 dated Oct 15, 1966, which had been entered exclusively in favour of one Shib Devi and sought declaration of her inheritance rights along with consequential possession.On March 9, 2004, the sub-judge court in Kishtwar passed a decree recognising her entitlement. However, the district judge reversed the decree on Nov 7, 2012, primarily on the grounds of limitation and failure to establish paternity.Justice Shahzad Azeem of the HC, while allowing the appeal filed by Themu, set aside the judgment of the district judge, Kishtwar, observing that limitation cannot be determined on presumptions and conjectures, particularly where the claimant was a minor when her rights were initially disputed and the defendants failed to establish when the cause of action actually arose.
Article Summary: The dispute dates back to Sept 14, 1982, when Themu, daughter of late Sonu, filed a civil suit claiming half share in land measuring 58 kanals and 11 marlas left behind by her father. She challenged mutation no. 43 dated Oct 15, 1966, which had been entered exclusively in favour of one Shib Devi.

Article Title: Set to expand cabinet, J&K CM Omar Abdullah asks hopefuls not to ‘mob or spam’ him
Article Text:
Omar was sworn in on Oct 16, 2024, along with five ministers,

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

SRINAGAR: J&K CM Omar Abdullah, who met lieutenant governor Manoj Sinha Saturday and announced that the much-anticipated cabinet expansion will take place next week, has urged party colleagues to stop sending him lengthy WhatsApp messages and book-length profiles seeking ministerial berths.He also advised them against knocking on his doors or that of his father and National Conference president, Dr Farooq Abdullah, to lobby for ministerial positions.After meeting Sinha, Omar told reporters he sought an appointment with him for next week so that he can make changes and expand his council of ministers.“Now that I have told you about the reshuffle, I want to make a request to my colleagues. There is no need to knock on Farooq Abdullah’s door, my door or anyone else’s door,” Omar said. “The decision about who will become a minister has been taken. I request my colleagues to be patient. First, it is in God’s hands and then we took the decision. Whoever is destined to become a minister will become one,” he said.“I am receiving so many WhatsApp messages, with people writing lengthy resumes and sending me entire book-length profiles. It is as if I do not know these people. They are sending me their complete biodata, as though I am not already familiar with them,” he said.“So please, do not send WhatsApp messages.”Omar was sworn in on Oct 16, 2024, along with five ministers, including deputy CM Surinder Choudhary. At present, three cabinet berths remain vacant.Under the norms, the strength of the council of ministers cannot exceed nine or 10% of the total strength of the 90-member assembly.Meanwhile, the opposition described Omar’s public “advice” to ministerial hopefuls as demeaning to the political class and called it as “the cult of self.”Leader of opposition, BJP’s Sunil Sharma, who has been claiming that NC will “implode” if Omar went ahead with cabinet expansion, said, “The CM is behaving like a king. He doesn’t like people visiting his home. He is out to demean his own MLAs and has repeatedly humiliated them inside and outside the Assembly.”Peoples Conference chairman Sajad Lone called Omar’s statement “the cult of self.” “I watched CM sahib talking to the media after meeting LG sahib. What a contemptuous and disdainful way of asking his party MLAs to not pester him for a ministerial berth. I honestly can’t believe these MLAs are comfortable with such belittling and humiliating remarks,” Lone said.“If you are unable to accommodate them in the cabinet, you can spare them the public humiliation,” he said.
Article Summary: J&K CM Omar Abdullah has urged party colleagues to stop sending him lengthy WhatsApp messages and book-length profiles seeking ministerial berths. He also advised them against knocking on his doors or that of his father and National Conference president, Dr Farooq Abdullah, to lobby for ministerial positions.

NEW DELHI: AISA president Neha Bora appeared before the special executive magistrate (SEM) at Mandir Marg Police Station on Saturday, a day after the Delhi High Court dismissed her plea challenging a police notice directing her to execute a Rs 10,000 bond with one surety to maintain peace during an inquiry.During the proceedings, the SEM directed the police to provide the relevant documents to Bora’s counsel and granted time to file a reply. The next hearing is scheduled for October 29.Advocate Abhik Chimni, commenting on the High Court’s judgment, said, "The High Court has dismissed the challenge to the show-cause notice. However, it has laid down important parameters, stating that all material relied upon to suggest a possible breach of peace must be provided to us. Today, we showed the judgment to the SEM, who gave us all the documents. We will examine them before the next hearing on the 29th. The court's findings are important as they uphold the right of detained persons to know the allegations against them and have a reasoned opportunity to reply. "Bora alleged that a group of “goons” was standing outside the Mandir Marg police station as she arrived to appear before the SEM court.“Police were not dispersing these goons, is this not a breach of peace?” she said.Earlier on Saturday, Bora said she would not sign the bond. "We don't have any conditions. We are not going to sign the bond," she said.The notice, issued on October 17 under Section 126 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS), directed Bora to appear before the magistrate and explain why she should not execute a personal bond of Rs 10,000 with one surety to maintain peace during the inquiry.Bora challenged the notice in the Delhi High Court, arguing that it was vague, factually incorrect and unsupported by material indicating a likelihood of a breach of peace. She alleged that the proceedings were a "colourable exercise of preventive powers to suppress peaceful dissent, in violation of Articles 19(1)(a), 19(1)(b) and 21 of Constitution".During a hearing on Thursday, her counsel argued that citizens did not need permission to hoist the national flag, responding to the police's allegation that Bora had hoisted it without valid permission.The proceedings relate to alleged sloganeering at Mandi House on October 16, repeated protests around Jantar Mantar despite prohibitory orders under Section 163 of the BNSS, and allegations that Bora had instigated people to join a demonstration at Connaught Place that day.Bora was taken into preventive detention on October 16 while on her way to participate in the Cockroach Janata Party's (CJP) 'Lehra Do Tiranga' march at Central Park in Connaught Place. She was released the following day.While dismissing her plea on Friday, the High Court directed the magistrate to provide Bora with all relevant material relied upon in the proceedings, allowing her an opportunity to respond to the allegations.

It recounts her personal journey, including her memories with Rajiv Gandhi and experiences from her younger days to the present.In the nearly two-minute video accompanying her first post on X, Sonia Gandhi recalled meeting Rajiv Gandhi at the Varsity Restaurant, a Greek eatery in Cambridge, England, where they were students.The video featured photographs of the couple and the restaurant where they first met."In a small Greek restaurant in Cambridge, my journey of love began. Rajiv and I created a world filled with love, laughter and memories. On 10th November, I share that world with you," she wrote in her post.Speaking in the video, the Congress MP recalled looking for Italian food while living in England, where she said the food available at the time did not suit her preferences."Food in England in those days was awful. In those days, you didn't have so many restaurants, you know, like you have today," she said.She explained that she was looking for a place serving food closer to what she was accustomed to, particularly Italian cuisine, when she discovered the Greek restaurant."And then, we discovered this place (Varsity Restaurant). It was a Greek restaurant where many European students, but also Indian students, used to go for their meals. And that is then where I met Rajiv in that very restaurant," she said.Recalling her first impression of Rajiv Gandhi, she said she felt almost immediately that he was someone she would want to spend her life with."When I first met him, I felt almost immediately that you know he was someone I would really love to be with. And, of course, I learned that it was the same for him," she said.Sonia Gandhi also recalled that a common friend introduced them. Then, you know, we became friends. Then going to parties with friends, or going to see sights, or… We went to a Valentine party where there were lots of students," she said.Describing what stood out to her about Rajiv Gandhi, she said his gentle nature had left a lasting impression."He was a very gentle-looking person. Of course, he was very good-looking. But that gentleness came through. So that was something which really touched me and struck me. So that, of course, I'll never forget when I first met him," she said.Sonia married Rajiv Gandhi on February 25, 1968.The upcoming memoir, Belonging: A Journey of Love, explores Sonia Gandhi's life, from her childhood in post-war Italy and her romance with Rajiv Gandhi to her move to India and the personal losses that shaped her life and relationship with her adopted country.Her debut on X comes two days after she joined Instagram on Thursday and shared a video offering a first look at the book.In her first Instagram post, she expressed gratitude at being able to share the preview with readers and described the memoir as a story of love, duty, loss and finding a place to belong."I look forward to sharing it with you," she wrote in the post.

Article Title: Presidential election today? Trump confuses India with Brazil, claims 125 million voted
Article Text:
Trump says "125 million Indians voted in presidential election today."

US President Donald Trump on Monday confused India with Brazil, claiming that 125 million people had voted in an Indian “presidential election”, while also questioning the integrity of the American voting system.In a post on Truth Social, Trump wrote, “125 Million People voted today in the first round of India’s Presidential Election. The results came out shortly after the vote closed, on the same day!”He then compared the alleged election results with the US electoral process, writing, “In Detroit, Philadelphia, California, and numerous other US Cities and States, the results, with much smaller numbers, will often take weeks to Rig, I mean, calculate. Voting in America is corrupt!!!”However, India did not hold a presidential election on Sunday. The President of India is elected indirectly by an electoral college and not through a direct nationwide popular vote.Trump's remarks came after Brazil held the first round of its presidential election on Sunday, with incumbent President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva and right-wing challenger Flávio Bolsonaro advancing to the October 25 runoff.With 99.99% of the votes counted, Bolsonaro secured 47.03% of the valid votes, while Lula received 45.16%, according to Brazil's Superior Electoral Court.The figure of around 125 million mentioned by Trump is close to Brazil's total valid votes, which stood at about 125.27 million, suggesting he may have confused the Brazilian election with India.Neither Bolsonaro nor Lula crossed the 50% threshold required to win in the first round, triggering the October 25 runoff, BBC reported.Flávio Bolsonaro, the son of former Brazilian president Jair Bolsonaro, outperformed expectations in the first round and finished ahead of Lula. His strong showing has raised the prospect of a shift to the right in Latin America's largest economy.Brazil has used electronic voting for decades, and electoral authorities said the first-round voting process proceeded smoothly.The Organization of American States' electoral observation mission said “the voting has been going smoothly and under adequate safety conditions.”The rapid announcement of results has also been cited as a strength of Brazil's electronic voting system.“When results take a lot of time, it creates an opening for people to cast doubt on the results, to say there’s been a problem,” Josemar Lauriano Pereira, a 46-year-old lawyer in Rio de Janeiro, told the Associated Press.Trump's post drew reactions on social media, with users pointing out that India does not elect its president through a direct popular vote.One user posted, “Trump living in a different world? Is a presidential election taking place in India? President Donald Trump made the incorrect claim that 125 million people voted in India's "presidential election" today.”Another said, “What is my blud Donald Trump smoking? Why is he mentioning India instead of Brazil when talking about the election?”
Article Summary: US President Donald Trump confused India with Brazil, claiming that 125 million people had voted in an Indian "presidential election" He also questioned the integrity of the American voting system. India did not hold a presidential election on Sunday. The President of India is elected indirectly by an electoral college.

She said the litigation had placed her under serious financial pressure, even though the company behind Klein’s lawsuit has since withdrawn the case.“I still owe $73K after it costing well over $100K.”She followed the post with a direct appeal to supporters.“Please donate to help cover my legal fees, so that I do not have to think about Ethan ever again.”Frogan also shared a link to her GoFundMe campaign, which seeks to raise $200,000. At the time of the report, the fundraiser had collected $45,491.In the campaign description, Frogan alleged that the dispute followed a prolonged period of harassment and said the lawsuit concerned her reaction to Klein’s video about Hasan Piker and herself, titled “Content Nuke - Hasan Piker.”The fundraiser is intended to cover legal bills linked to the complaint, possible counterclaims and other expenses, including lost wages and damages arising from the litigation.The legal dispute began in June 2025, when Ethan Klein accused Frogan and fellow online personalities Denims and Kacey “Kaceytron” of copyright infringement over reaction content related to his video.On September 8, 2026, Ted Entertainment, Inc., Klein’s company, voluntarily dismissed the proceedings without prejudice. This means the company may be able to bring the case again, so the dismissal does not necessarily end the dispute permanently.Frogan addressed the development in a September 9 post on X, expressing hope that the decision would bring the prolonged legal fight to a close.“On September 8, 2026, I woke up to the news that Ethan Klein had voluntarily dismissed his lawsuit against me after more than a year,” Frogan wrote.She also acknowledged that the dismissal could leave the door open for the lawsuit to be filed again.“Of course, I want to be hopeful that it means the end of the lawsuit, which has taken an enormous toll on me,” she added.Frogan has maintained that her use of Klein’s video qualified as fair use and thanked those who supported her throughout the proceedings. For now, the fundraiser highlights the costs she says remain even after the legal action was withdrawn.
Article Summary: Twitch streamer Morgan Frogan is asking supporters for financial help after a lengthy copyright dispute with YouTuber Ethan Klein. Frogan says she has already spent more than $100,000 on legal costs and wants to settle the remaining amount so she can move forward. Her fundraising appeal has drawn fresh attention to the personal and financial consequences of online disputes that escalate into legal battles.

His initiative aimed to give student-athletes from underserved communities a fair chance to compete, build connections and explore careers linked to golf. By including boys and girls from different backgrounds, Curry hoped to make the sport more inclusive while helping young players discover their potential both on and off the course.Curry introduced UNDERRATED in 2019 to celebrate people who often go unnoticed despite their talent and determination. The expansion into golf addressed a sport where access to courses, coaching and competitive events can be limited for many communities.Explaining the thinking behind the move, Curry said, “I created UNDERRATED back in 2019 with the goal of celebrating the underdog,” said Stephen Curry. “UNDERRATED is a mindset, a motivation, a calling, a compliment. With this inspiration, I am excited to expand the brand into UNDERRATED Golf, which happens to be one of the most inaccessible sports for underrepresented individuals across the globe.UNDERRATED Golf will provide equity, access and opportunity, recognizing the instrumental role the sport plays as one of the greatest vehicles and connectors for life successes. ”The programme was designed to give young golfers access to courses and competitions they might otherwise struggle to reach. It also aimed to address gender inequality by ensuring female players received opportunities comparable to those available to boys.Beyond competition, UNDERRATED Golf planned to introduce participants to professional networks, learning sessions and potential career paths. These experiences could help young athletes understand how golf can open doors in business and other industries, even if they do not become professional players.Will Lowery, an UNDERRATED Golf professional and tour ambassador, stressed the importance of making the sport accessible to young people from underserved backgrounds.“We are dedicated to enacting real change by creating lanes for boys and girls from underserved communities to gain access to the sport,” said Will Lowery, UNDERRATED Golf Professional and Tour Ambassador. “UNDERRATED Golf provides equity, access and opportunity, recognizing the instrumental role the sport plays as one of the greatest vehicles and connectors for life success—from relationship building to career endeavors. We are focused on equal representation of all genders, while being a force multiplier for them to realize their potential and positively impact the sport—from skill on the course to competing in major tournaments and pursuing leadership roles across industries.”In its first year, the UNDERRATED Golf Tour planned to select 24 standout boys and girls to compete for the Curry Cup at the season-ending championship. The initiative also aimed to expand its reach over time and identify promising talent from more communities.Curry's approach reflects a broader goal: giving young people the resources and confidence to succeed, regardless of their starting point. Through UNDERRATED Golf, he sought to make opportunity a more important part of the sport's future.

Article Title: FBI detains gangster Himanshu Bhau, India may get custody soon

Himanshu's major cirmes





NEW DELHI: Himanshu Bhau, one of north India's most wanted gangsters, is learnt to have been detained in the US, after a four-year-long manhunt. Subject of a red notice from the Interpol, Bhau, a rival of Lawrence Bishnoi group, is wanted for multiple cases off shootings, killings and multi-crore extortions in Delhi and Haryana.Bhau, sources said, was apprehended by FBI in Las Vegas/Nevada region following inputs from Indian agencies. He is likely to be handed over to Indian law enforcement agencies, who have been chasing him since 2022, in the coming days, sources said.In his early twenties, Bhau is one of north India's most notorious young fugitives, heading an organised crime syndicate. He has been a headache for cops in Delhi, Haryana and Rajasthan with back-to-back killings, including three sensational murders in Delhi, this year."He belongs to Ritoli in the Rohtak district of Haryana and had got involved in crimes while still in school. He first entered police records in 2020 following a botched killing attempt involving a localized dispute in his native village," an investigator recalled.Since he was a minor at the time of apprehension, cops detained him and sent him to a juvenile observation home in Hisar. However, his stay there was brief; he engineered an audacious escape from the facility, casting aside any prospect of rehabilitation and plunging headfirst into a career of violent crime that soon expanded far beyond rural Haryana.Operating in close coordination with seasoned syndicates, including the Neeraj Bawana and Naveen Bali gangs, Bhau rapidly built a formidable network spanning Rohtak, Jhunjhunu, Sonipat, and the National Capital Region of Delhi.As law enforcement agencies closed in on his local footprints, including a series of high-profile murders in his home district in March 2022, he managed to orchestrate an escape from the country."In 2022, he executed three killings in a span of 24 days in March. The same year, using a passport obtained through fraudulent documents, Bhau slipped across international borders, initially fleeing to Dubai before moving on to European safe havens like Portugal, from where he continued to remotely direct his syndicate," said an investigator.Despite being a fugitive with Red Corner Notices and heavy cash rewards issued by multiple police jurisdictions and the National Investigation Agency, he leveraged encrypted messaging applications to command local shooters.He is suspected to have reached US through the "Dunkey Route" in late 2024-early 2025.His syndicate has claimed responsibility for a string of high-profile shootings, extortions, and contract killings that terrorised businessmen and shook law enforcement.Among his syndicate's most brazen operations was the daring killing of a rival at a prominent fast-food chain outlet in West Delhi's Rajouri Garden.His network has also targeted commercial establishments, unleashing dozens of rounds of gunfire at car showrooms in Naraina and Tilak Nagar alongside multi-million rupee extortion demands directed at builders, real estate developers, and local traders across Delhi-NCR.
Article Summary: Himanshu Bhau, one of north India's most wanted gangsters, is learnt to have been detained in the US. He is likely to be handed over to Indian law enforcement agencies, who have been chasing him since 2022, in the coming days.

India created a major T20 International record during their thrilling four-wicket win over New Zealand in Christchurch on Saturday. While the team celebrated a memorable victory, another achievement went largely unnoticed.India became the first team to play 300 men's T20 Internationals and also recorded their 200th win in the format. They reached the milestone in style, chasing down New Zealand's 180/5 with one ball to spare after losing five wickets for just 70 runs.The victory was made possible by an unbeaten 51 off 26 balls from Tilak Varma and an unbeaten 26 off 13 balls from Nitish Kumar Reddy. Their 69-run partnership for the seventh wicket took India to 181/6 in 19.5 overs.India have played 300 T20Is between 2006 and 2026, winning 200 matches, losing 83, tying seven and finishing 10 without a result. Their win-loss ratio stands at 2.409, which means they have won more than twice as many matches as they have lost.Pakistan have played the most T20Is overall, with 304 matches, but have recorded 176 wins. India are ahead of them in the number of victories despite playing four fewer matches.New Zealand, India's opponents in Christchurch, have played 269 T20Is and won 135. South Africa and England complete the top five teams on the list of total wins.India's 200 wins put them well ahead of the other major teams. Here is how the leading teams have performed in men's T20Is.Figures cover the period up to 2026, as provided.India's 200th T20I win did not come easily. Chasing 181, they were struggling at 70/5 in 10.5 overs after New Zealand captain Mitchell Santner took control with the ball.Sanju Samson fell for 14, while Vaibhav Sooryavanshi managed only four. Abhishek Sharma scored 27 off 21 balls before Santner dismissed him. The left-arm spinner then removed captain Shreyas Iyer for seven and Axar Patel for 11, leaving India in serious trouble.Naman Dhir gave India some hope with an aggressive 31 off 17 balls, including a four and three sixes. But his dismissal in the 15th over left the visitors needing another strong partnership.Tilak took responsibility and played a calm yet attacking innings. He struck six fours and a six, reaching his half-century in 25 balls.Nitish Kumar Reddy provided the perfect support, scoring an unbeaten 26 off 13 balls. The pair added 69 runs without being separated in just 30 balls.Their partnership changed the match and took India to 181/6 in 19.5 overs. India won by four wickets, with one ball remaining.Santner was New Zealand's best bowler, taking four wickets for 21 runs in four overs. However, his effort was not enough to stop India's record-breaking victory.Earlier, New Zealand recovered from a poor start to post 180/5 in their 20 overs. India's bowlers made early inroads. Arshdeep Singh dismissed Tim Seifert for seven, Prince Yadav removed Finn Allen for 16, and Bhuvneshwar Kumar sent back Daryl Mitchell for six.New Zealand were reduced to 41/3, but Glenn Phillips and Bevon Jacobs rebuilt the innings with a 116-run partnership for the fourth wicket.Phillips scored 70 off 43 balls, hitting four fours and four sixes. He brought up his half-century in 33 balls before Arshdeep dismissed him in the 18th over.Jacobs made 58 off 46 balls, including five fours and a six, before Nitish Reddy removed him. Michael Bracewell then added a late burst with a four and a six as New Zealand finished at 180/5.Arshdeep was India's leading bowler with figures of 2/33. Prince took one wicket for 30 runs, while Bhuvneshwar finished with 1/50. Axar conceded 28 runs in four overs without taking a wicket, and Reddy claimed 1/31 in three overs.India's bowlers had kept New Zealand to a manageable total, but the hosts' strong middle-order partnership ensured the visitors had a challenging target. Tilak and Reddy eventually completed the chase, giving India a landmark win.
Article Summary: India became the first team to play 300 men's T20 Internationals. They reached the milestone in style, chasing down New Zealand's 180/5 with one ball to spare. The victory was made possible by an unbeaten 51 off 26 balls from Tilak Varma and an unbeaten 26 off 13 balls from Nitish Kumar Reddy.

Article Title: In 1996, a New York couple bought their home believing a tree line marked the boundary; 30 years later, an appeals court revived a privacy claim over cameras filming their backyard and daughter
Article Text:
Dalys built a chain-link fence in 2006, while Rileys installed their own fence about two feet away in 2011. (AI image)

Disagreement over trees led to surveillance cameras

Why court allowed privacy claim to continue

What happened to the original property dispute?

A New York couple who bought their home in 1996 believing that a line of trees marked the boundary with their neighbour's property have spent years fighting over the same stretch of land. What began as a disagreement over where one property ended and the other began eventually involved allegations of trespass and surveillance cameras recording their backyard.Nearly 30 years after the purchase, a New York appeals court has revived the couple's privacy claim after they alleged that their neighbours' cameras captured thousands of images and videos, including footage of their swimming pool and young daughter.According to details of the case available on Justia , the ruling, delivered on Thursday, concerns Timothy J. Riley and his co-plaintiff, who own a home in the Town of Malta, Saratoga County, and their neighbours, John C Daly and his co-defendant. Both properties are part of a four-plot residential development, with the Rileys living on the northern side and the Dalys to the south.The Rileys purchased their property from the developer in December 1996.At the time, they understood that the trees between the two plots marked the boundary. The original neighbour appeared to share that understanding. He watched them maintain the wooded area on their side and later helped them build a garage about 15 feet from the trees.Things began to change in 2004 when the neighbour sold his property to the Dalys. Two years later, the new owners built a chain-link fence between the tree line and the Rileys' garage. The Rileys believed the fence stood on their land. In 2011, they installed their own fence about two feet away. Over time, the disagreement grew into a dispute involving approximately 230 feet of the boundary.By 2018, the dispute had reached the courts. Both households accused each other of wrongdoing in the contested area. The Rileys wanted the boundary they had recognised for years to be legally accepted, while the Dalys maintained that the land belonged to them.But the disagreement was no longer limited to fences and property lines. The Dalys had also installed surveillance cameras, which became a major part of the Rileys' lawsuit.The Dalys told the court that they had installed the cameras to monitor their property following alleged incidents of trespass, theft and harassment. They maintained that the purpose was to prevent further problems, not to harass their neighbours.The Rileys, however, raised concerns about what the cameras were recording. They submitted photographs showing their backyard and swimming pool, including an image of their daughter, who was a minor.They also claimed that information obtained from one of the cameras and during the legal proceedings showed that thousands of photographs or videos had been captured. According to them, the recordings extended beyond the disputed strip of land into other parts of their backyard.New York has a law that protects homeowners against certain types of unwanted surveillance by neighbours. It allows people to seek damages if cameras are installed on adjoining property to record activities in their backyard without written permission and with the intention of harassing, alarming or threatening them.The lower court had earlier dismissed their privacy claim. However, the appeals court disagreed, finding that the photographs and allegations about the recordings raised questions that needed further examination and reinstated the Rileys' invasion of privacy claim.While the cameras became an important issue, the question that started the disagreement remained unresolved: Where exactly was the boundary between the two homes?The Rileys argued that the tree line should be recognised because it had been treated as the boundary for years. Under New York law, a boundary accepted by neighbouring owners for more than 10 years can, in certain circumstances, become legally recognised.However, the court found that the Rileys had not provided enough evidence to establish that both households had accepted the trees as the boundary for the required period. The Dalys' decision to build a fence on the Rileys' claimed side of the trees also raised doubts about such an agreement.The Dalys, meanwhile, relied on land surveys to support their ownership claim. But the Rileys pointed out differences between the surveys, arguing that these could shift the boundary by approximately 10 feet.They also alleged that wooden survey stakes and the original natural boundary had been removed before a surveyor inspected the property in 2018.The appeals court found that these differences could not be ignored. It thus overturned the lower court's decision to settle the boundary according to the Dalys' survey.Another disagreement involved allegations that the Rileys had cut or removed trees from the disputed land. The judges found that this issue also required further examination because ownership of the area had not been conclusively established. The case will therefore require further proceedings to resolve the competing property claims and determine whether the alleged surveillance violated the Rileys' privacy rights.
Article Summary: New York couple bought their home in 1996 believing that a line of trees marked the boundary with their neighbour's property. The Rileys wanted the boundary they had recognised for years to be legally accepted, while the Dalys maintained that the land belonged to them. Over time, the disagreement grew into a dispute involving approximately 230 feet of the boundary. The Dalys had also installed surveillance cameras, which became a major part of the lawsuit. Both households accused each other of wrongdoing in the contested area.

Article Title: A 27-year-old Minnesota man saw a school bus carrying 19 children rolling with its doors open, jumped aboard despite never driving one and stopped it after the driver suffered a medical emergency
Article Text:
Ahmed spotted the struggling driver and raced toward the slow-moving bus, travelling about 10 mph.

A bus without a driver in control

Protecting students

A situation he never expected

Driver released from hospital

A routine afternoon in St. Paul took a frightening turn when a school bus began moving through the streets with its driver incapacitated. With 19 middle school students on board and no one apparently in control of the vehicle, a nearby business owner found himself facing a split-second decision, run toward the bus or watch it continue down the road.According to ABC News, Ebro Ahmed, 27, was taking a break outside his family-owned business, Ya Bricks Snacks & Tobacco, in the Dayton's Bluff neighbourhood when he noticed the Battle Creek Middle School bus travelling with its doors open. What he saw inside prompted him to act immediately.According to ABC News and the New York Post, Ahmed noticed that something was wrong with the driver as the bus moved slowly through the area. The vehicle was reportedly travelling at around 10 mph, giving Ahmed enough time to catch up.He ran toward the moving bus and climbed aboard. Ahmed had never driven a school bus before, but with the children still inside and the vehicle continuing forward, he attempted to bring it under control. His first attempt did not go entirely as planned. He reversed the bus instead of parking. After switching to neutral and setting the parking brake, the bus stopped.Ahmed faced the children and driver when the bus stopped. He helped the disabled driver and told students to call 911. The 19 students were not physically injured, although the sudden incident left some of them frightened. Reports described children preparing to call 911 and reacting anxiously as the situation unfolded.Ahmed's actions prevented the bus from continuing uncontrolled through the neighbourhood, turning what could have become a far more serious incident into an emergency response rather than a potential crash. Fox34 reported that the incident occurred Monday and involved a contracted route serving Battle Creek Middle School.Ahmed later acknowledged that he had no formal training in operating a school bus. His response instead came from trying to remain calm and recalling things he had seen before. Among the unexpected influences he credited was the medical drama Grey's Anatomy, along with videos encountered online. Rather than panic, he tried to concentrate on the immediate problem and work through the controls.The St. Paul Public Schools district said the driver's medical emergency likely caused delays for students returning home. Some children were also upset by what had happened, prompting the district's mental health team to check in with students following the incident.The bus driver was taken to a hospital following the medical emergency and was later released to recover at home, according to school officials, states the ABC News report.Ahmed said the episode was particularly personal because he could easily imagine the children being members of his own family. His decision to intervene, therefore, was less about recognition and more about protecting a group of children who suddenly found themselves in an unpredictable and potentially dangerous situation.The incident has since drawn widespread attention online, with Ahmed being praised for his quick response. What began as an ordinary break outside a neighbourhood business ended with an untrained bystander taking control of a moving school bus and helping ensure that all 19 students made it through a frightening journey safely.Images Courtesy: ABC News
Article Summary: Ebro Ahmed, 27, was taking a break outside his family-owned business in St. Paul, Minnesota, when he saw the bus with its doors open. The driver was taken to hospital for a medical emergency and later released to recover at home. The 19 students were not physically injured, although the sudden incident left them frightened.

Article Title: How did Jaylen Brown step up without LeBron James? Philadelphia 76ers extend unbeaten start against Milwaukee Bucks
Article Text:
How did Jaylen Brown step up without LeBron James?(Getty Images)

Jaylen Brown takes charge as Philadelphia beats Milwaukee

Joel Embiid's triple-double helps the Sixers reach 3-0

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Jaylen Brown turned 30 on October 24, 2026, and gave the Philadelphia 76ers another reason to celebrate. With LeBron James sitting out their game against the Milwaukee Bucks, Brown took on a bigger scoring role and finished with 27 points. Philadelphia won 127-116 to improve to 3-0 in the 2026-27 NBA season.Brown's performance came alongside a big night from Joel Embiid, who recorded a triple-double. The Sixers had enough scoring options to handle James' absence and keep their unbeaten start going.Brown gave Philadelphia the scoring boost it needed without James. He attacked defenders in the mid-range, used his strength to create room for jump shots and found ways to finish near the basket. He also connected from three-point range, making it difficult for Milwaukee to settle into a defensive rhythm.The 76ers did not need Brown to carry the entire offense. Tyrese Maxey scored 26 points and added four assists, while VJ Edgecombe finished with 17 points and 12 rebounds. Their contributions helped Philadelphia maintain its offensive pressure throughout the game.James sat out because of lower back pain management, according to the Associated Press.The 41-year-old had averaged 15.5 points and 9.5 rebounds in his first two games with Philadelphia. The team had won both contests, beating the New York Knicks and Cleveland Cavaliers.His absence gave Brown more opportunities to create his own shots. Brown's ability to score without needing a pass to set him up offered Philadelphia another option when Milwaukee tried to disrupt its offense.The Bucks still made the Sixers work for the win. Philadelphia had some uneven stretches, but its three-point shooting improved after the team shot below 30% from beyond the arc in each of its first two games. Brown helped keep the offense moving as the Sixers worked to close out the contest.While Brown led the scoring story, Embiid controlled much of Philadelphia's offense. He finished with 28 points, 11 rebounds and 10 assists, recording the 10th triple-double of his NBA career.Embiid scored in the post and created opportunities for teammates when Milwaukee sent extra defenders his way. His passing helped Brown and Maxey find room to attack, giving Philadelphia more ways to punish the Bucks' defense.Edgecombe also made an early impact with three three-pointers. Foul trouble limited his playing time, but his rebounding added another dimension to his performance. He also helped create a key second-chance opportunity for Embiid late in the game.Dean Wade made his Sixers debut after missing the first two games with an ankle sprain. He hit a corner three-pointer on his first touch and finished with two three-pointers and three steals. His defensive work gave head coach Nick Nurse another useful option.Kentavious Caldwell-Pope added 12 points off the bench and made several important defensive plays. Jabari Walker also contributed on the glass before leaving the game with an injury.Philadelphia's 127-116 victory moved it to 3-0 after wins over the Knicks, Cavaliers and Bucks. The result also gave the team a positive start to a demanding weekend schedule.The Sixers will host the Detroit Pistons on October 25, the second game of their back-to-back. James had already indicated that he would play in only one of the two games that weekend. After beating Milwaukee without him, Philadelphia will look to carry its winning start into the next matchup.
Article Summary: Philadelphia 76ers beat Milwaukee Bucks 127-116 to go 3-0 in 2026-27 NBA season. LeBron James sat out game because of lower back pain management. Jaylen Brown scored 27 points, while Joel Embiid recorded a triple-double.

Article Title: Cheered in Chhota Udepur, but Vadodara shuts stage to Muslim who played Lakshmana for 14 years
Article Text:
Abid Sheikh, an actor in Vadodara, was excluded from performing in Ram Leela due to his religion.





VADODARA: On Dussehra , Abid Sheikh drew applause in tribal Chhota Udepur for bringing the characters of Kevat and Meghnad alive on stage in a Ram Leela.In Vadodara, however, the city he calls home, the 39-year-old was unable to perform in the Ram Leela he had been associated with for nearly 14 years, after objections to his participation over his religion by right-wing groups.The contrast has left Sheikh, a science graduate who grew up fascinated by the Ramayana, grappling with an unexpected rejection from a tradition that had become an integral part of his life.For years, Sheikh played Laxman and Bharat in the Ram Leela organised by the North India Cultural Association (NICA) at Polo Ground during Dussehra. He learnt his dialogues, rehearsed for weeks and earned appreciation from audiences. His family, too, shared his commitment, giving up non-vegetarian food during the rehearsal period until the festival concluded.But the welcome he had long received on stage in Vadodara changed last year when some right-wing activists turned up during rehearsals and objected to his casting because he was a Muslim.“I played different roles in Ram Leela for around 14 years and was showered with love and appreciation by the audience.Last year, some activists suddenly turned up during rehearsals and objected to my casting because of my religion. I was shocked, as I never expected this,” Sheikh told TOI.He said the activists pressured the organisers to drop him. This year, he was not invited to perform in the Vadodara production.“Ram Leela had become a part of my life, but they did not want me anywhere near the stage,” he said.The rejection was particularly painful because his association with the epic began in childhood. After watching a cartoon based on the Ramayana, Sheikh developed a fascination for Laxman. An opportunity to perform in a school Ram Leela gave him his first taste of acting, and he continued playing characters from the epic for years.Shashikant Das, director, NICA, told TOI: “Sheikh is such a good actor and he is an ardent fan of Ramayan. He chants Hanuman Chalisa. But Bajrang Dal activists came last year and protested against his role. I argued and fought in Sheikh’s defence.”“But the management came under pressure. So, this time he wasn’t invited for the Ram Leela. It’s sad that we lost a good actor like him,” Das said and pointed out that those preparing the giant effigies of Ravana, Meghnad and Kumbhakarna at Polo Ground are also Muslim artists from Uttar Pradesh.
Article Summary: Abid Sheikh, an actor in Vadodara, was excluded from performing in Ram Leela due to his religion. Right-wing activists turned up during rehearsals and objected to his casting because he was a Muslim. He said the activists pressured the organisers to drop him.

Article Title: Amid political buzz, actor Dhanush to address women's wing following fan club restructuring
Article Text:
Tamil actor Dhanush (File Photo)

(With inputs from PTI)





CHENNAI: Amid speculation about a possible political entry, Tamil actor Dhanush is scheduled to meet the women's wing of his recently reorganised fan association at a private college in Chennai on Sunday.The meeting comes after the actor's fan club, formerly known as Dhanush Narpani Mandram, was renamed Dhanush Narpani Iyakkam and restructured as a welfare movement.In Tamil, “Iyakkam” means an organisation/movement, and the renaming has drawn attention since chief minister C Joseph Vijay renamed his fan club into All India Thalapathy Vijay Makkal Iyakkam in 2009, a first step towards politics.The change was formally adopted at a recent meeting of the association's executives in Coimbatore. The organisation has also unveiled a new logo featuring the actor with folded hands against a large red star, enclosed within a circular red-and-white border.Dhanush has not made any official announcement about entering politics or forming a political party. However, the restructuring of his fan association has fuelled discussions in Tamil Nadu about the organisation's future role, including its focus on coordinated social service initiatives.For many women attending Sunday's meeting, however, the immediate attraction was the opportunity to see the actor in person.Several fans travelled to the venue despite heavy rain in Chennai."My name is Sophia, we are coming from Villivakkam. We were invited here for an event, but our main reason for coming in this pouring rain is to see Dhanush sir," one of the fans told news agency PTI."We don't know what he is going to talk about today, but we are confident it will be useful for us," she added.Hannah, who travelled from Perambur, said it would be her first opportunity to see the actor in person."I came here to see Dhanush. I have seen his movies many times, but this is the first time I am going to see him live. I am so eager and excited to watch him," she said.Bhanupriya, a fan from Triplicane, also spoke about her longstanding admiration for the actor."I am a big fan of his. From childhood, I watch all his movies. I am so excited to see him."
Article Summary: Tamil actor Dhanush is scheduled to meet the women's wing of his fan association. The meeting comes after the actor's fan club was restructured as a welfare movement. The restructuring has fuelled discussions in Tamil Nadu about the organisation's future role.
